Item battery table from a survey design

Source: R/table_battery_svy.R
table_battery_svy.Rd

The design twin of table_battery(): a battery of items answered on one common scale, one row per item and one column per level, with row percentages estimated from a survey::svydesign() or survey::as.svrepdesign() object instead of a data frame.

Every statistic is survey's. survey::svymean() estimates the percentages of each item, and, with by, survey::svychisq() tests each item against the group, Rao-Scott corrected by default, the p-values adjusted for the family of the items by Holm's method.

The rows, the columns, levels, top, sort and the outputs are those of table_battery().

Usage

table_battery_svy(
  design,
  select,
  by = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  top = NULL,
  sort = "",
  drop_na = TRUE,
  show_n = TRUE,
  chisq_statistic = c("F", "Chisq", "Wald", "adjWald", "saddlepoint"),
  p_value = NULL,
  p_adjust = "holm",
  labels = getOption("spicy.var_labels", FALSE),
  note_labels = NULL,
  percent_digits = 1,
  p_digits = 3,
  decimal_mark = ".",
  align = c("decimal", "center", "right"),
  title = NULL,
  note = NULL,
  note_add = NULL,
  output = c("default", "data.frame", "long", "tinytable", "gt", "flextable", "excel",
    "clipboard", "word"),
  excel_path = NULL,
  excel_sheet = NULL,
  clipboard_delim = "\t",
  word_path = NULL,
  style = NULL
)

Arguments

design

A survey design: survey::svydesign() or survey::as.svrepdesign().

select

The items of the battery, one column of the design per item, in tidyselect syntax or as a character vector of names. Their order is the order of the rows, unless sort sorts them. The by column and the design's own columns (its weights, replicate weights, clusters and finite population corrections) are not part of the selection: a selection helper skips them, and naming one is an error. The items share one scale, read as in table_battery().

by

Optional grouping column, unquoted or as a string. Factor levels keep their declared order; any other column is sorted, as in table_categorical(). Rows with a missing by are removed from the whole table, and the note gives their count ("Missing values removed: sex (2)."); a by that no observation holds is an error (class spicy_invalid_data).

levels

The scale: the levels to show, in the order of the columns, as in table_battery(). NULL (the default) reads the scale from the items, under the rules of the section Items and levels of table_battery(). Given, levels is the scale: a level that no item holds shows at 0, and any other answer is left out of the domain, and the note names it.

top

The levels the summary column adds up, for example top = c("Strongly agree", "Agree"). The column follows the levels; its header is the list of the levels joined by " + ", in the order of top, and its value is the sum of their percentages. Each entry must be one of the levels shown (see levels); another value is an error. Without by, a top of one level would repeat the column of that level, and is an error. NULL (the default) adds no column.

sort

The order of the rows, in the suffix grammar of freq() and table_multiresponse(), + for increasing and - for decreasing order:

  • "" (the default): the order of select;

  • "+" / "-": by the summary column of top, or, without top, by the first level shown;

  • "top+" / "top-": by the summary column (needs top);

  • "name+" / "name-": by the label of the item, in the C locale, the same on every platform (capitals before lower case);

  • "<level>+" / "<level>-": by the percentage of a level shown, for example sort = "Strongly agree-".

With by, the percentages are those of all the groups together. Items with the same value keep the order of select, and an item without data sorts last. The keywords are read first: "name+" sorts on the labels even when a level is called "name", and "top+" on the summary column even when a level is called "top". A level or a keyword without its direction ("Agree", "top") has two readings, and is an error that gives both. Any other value is an error.

drop_na

Logical. If TRUE (the default), the missing answers to an item leave its domain: its percentages are estimated on its valid answers, and its n counts them. If FALSE, a last column of missing answers ("(Missing)") follows the levels, and the domain of each item takes every row of non-zero weight, its missing answers included.

show_n

Logical. If TRUE (the default), each row (each group block under by) ends with n, the observed (unweighted) count of the respondents its percentages are estimated on.

chisq_statistic

Statistic for survey::svychisq(): "F" (default), "Chisq", "Wald", "adjWald" or "saddlepoint". "saddlepoint" is refused on a replicate-weights design: survey computes its p-value without the denominator degrees of freedom there, so it comes out too small.

p_value

Logical or NULL. With by, NULL (the default) and TRUE show the p column of the item tests; FALSE removes it from every output. Ignored without by, with a warning when TRUE.

p_adjust

Multiple-comparison adjustment of the p column, applied to the family of the items tested: "holm" (the default), "none", or another method of stats::p.adjust() ("hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BH" / "fdr", "BY"). See the section Multiple-comparison adjustment of table_battery(). Typing it when the table has no test to adjust (no by, or p_value = FALSE) is an error.

labels

How each variable is named in the table: in the rows, in the title, and in the notes. Four forms:

  • labels = FALSE shows the column name.

  • labels = TRUE shows the column's label attribute (as set by haven, labelled, or label_from_names()) when it is present, not NA, and not empty, and the column name otherwise.

  • labels = c(bmi = "Body mass index"), a named character vector, gives the columns it names these labels. Every other column follows options(spicy.var_labels): its name when the option is unset or FALSE, its label attribute when it is TRUE.

  • labels = var_labels(bmi = "BMI (kg/m2)") gives the columns it names these labels, and every other column its label attribute, whatever the option says. var_labels() alone is labels = TRUE.

A name that matches no column of the table warns (class spicy_unknown_name) and is left out, so one vector can still serve every table of a project. The default reads options(spicy.var_labels), and a TRUE or FALSE typed in the call wins over it. Any other value, NULL included, is an error. A variable label documents the data file; a published table carries the wording you set here. note_labels gives a variable a shorter label in the title and the notes.

note_labels

The label a variable takes where the table names it in a sentence, in the title and in the notes, in place of the one labels gives it: a named character vector, note_labels = c(sex = "sex at birth"), or a var_labels() object, which reads as one. labels can then name a row with a whole question while the note says "Missing values removed: sex at birth (2).". The rows, the column headers and the spanners keep the labels of labels, and so do the title and the notes for a variable note_labels does not name. A name that matches no column warns and is left out, as in labels, and NULL (the default) renames nothing. A note label that another variable of the table shows is an error (class spicy_label_collision): choose another one, or relabel the other variable.

percent_digits

Number of digits for percentages in report outputs. Defaults to 1. A whole number: a fraction is an error, as for every *_digits argument.

p_digits

Integer >= 1. Number of decimal places used to render p-values in the p column (default: 3, the APA Publication Manual standard). Both the displayed precision and the small-p threshold derive from this argument: p_digits = 3 prints .045 and <.001; p_digits = 4 prints .0451 and <.0001. Leading zeros are always stripped, following APA convention.

decimal_mark

The decimal mark, a single character: "." (the default) or "," in most styles; the Lancet style of spicy_style() uses the middle dot.

align

Horizontal alignment of the numeric columns in the console and in the rendered outputs: "decimal" (the default), "center", or "right", as in table_categorical().

title

The table title. NULL (the default) gives "Item battery", followed by "by" and the by variable under the labels contract (or its label in note_labels); a single string replaces it, and FALSE removes it, as in table_multiresponse().

note

The table note. NULL (the default) builds it, opening with "Note.": the design, the direction of the percentages, the base, the levels left out, the rows removed and the items without data, then the tests and the sentences of note_add. A single string replaces it, and FALSE removes it, as in table_battery().

note_add

Sentences to add to the note: a character vector of one or more strings, each printed as typed (no period is added) and joined to the note by a space. They close its paragraph, after the definitions of the abbreviations and before the legend of the stars, in every output and in attr(x, "note"), and the sentences the table writes stay. With a string in note, they follow it, so a wrapper can add a house sentence to every table while one table replaces its note. An NA or an empty string is an error, and so is note_add with note = FALSE, which leaves no note to add to.

output

Output format. One of:

  • "default" (an ASCII table object, printed when the call is bare)

  • "data.frame" (the displayed table, numeric)

  • "long" (a long numeric data.frame)

  • "tinytable" (requires tinytable)

  • "gt" (requires gt)

  • "flextable" (requires flextable)

  • "excel" (requires openxlsx2)

  • "clipboard" (requires clipr)

  • "word" (requires flextable and officer)

excel_path

Path for output = "excel", ending in ".xlsx", in a directory that exists. Defaults to NULL.

excel_sheet

Sheet name for Excel export. NULL (the default) uses "Item battery".

clipboard_delim

Delimiter for clipboard text export. Defaults to "\t". A cell holding the delimiter itself, a double quote or a line break is quoted RFC 4180-style, so the grid survives whatever delimiter you choose.

word_path

File path for output = "word". Defaults to NULL.

style

A journal style: a theme name ("jama", "nejm", "lancet", "annals", "apa", "aer"), a spicy_style() object, or NULL (the default). A style only changes DEFAULTS – any argument you pass explicitly wins over it. Set options(spicy.style = ) for document-wide scope. A theme covers numeric formatting, the word that opens the note and the abbreviations the note defines, not full editorial conformity; ?spicy_style lists the exact rules each one encodes and the official document they come from. An unknown name is an error.

Value

Depends on output, as in table_battery():

  • "default": a spicy_battery_svy_table (a data.frame subclass), printed when the call is bare.

  • "data.frame": the displayed table with its numbers, the shape of table_battery(): variable, label, one percentage per level shown, (Missing) under drop_na = FALSE, the summary column of top, n, each prefixed with the group under by, and p.

  • "long": one row per item, group and level, with variable, label, group (with by), level, .row_role, n (the observed count) and pct (the estimated percentage), and, when the tests ran, test_type (the statistic of survey::svychisq()), p.value and p_unadjusted under an adjustment.

  • "tinytable", "gt", "flextable": the rendered table object.

  • "excel" / "word": writes to disk and returns the file path invisibly.

  • "clipboard": copies the table and returns the display data.frame invisibly.

as_structured() and inline() read the default object as they read that of table_battery(): inline(x, item, "Yes", "pct"), with model = "<group>" under by.

Estimation

The percentage of a level is survey::svymean() of the item on its domain: within the group under by, the rows of non-zero weight whose answer is a level shown. The domain is cut from the design with [, which keeps its strata, clusters and finite population corrections. Under drop_na = FALSE, the missing answers are a level of their own and stay in the domain. An answer that levels leaves out is outside the domain either way. An item that offers one level is 100% by arithmetic: survey does not estimate a variable with one level.

A cell that survey cannot estimate, most often because a stratum holds a single primary sampling unit under its default options(survey.lonely.psu = "fail"), shows a dash: the function warns once, quoting survey's messages (class spicy_svy_estimation_failed), and the note says what the dash means. A warning of survey's own, such as the one on a stratum with a single primary sampling unit in a domain under options(survey.adjust.domain.lonely = TRUE), is said once per table, with the number of times survey raised it.

n is the observed count of the domain, the respondents and not the estimated population, as in table_categorical_svy(). A row with a missing by leaves the table, and the note gives their count.

Tests

With by, each item is tested against the group by survey::svychisq() with chisq_statistic, on its answers on the levels shown, the missing answers left out whatever drop_na; the levels and the groups without an answer leave the test, as in table_battery(). The default "F" is the Pearson chi-squared with the Rao-Scott second-order correction, referred to the design degrees of freedom. The p-values are adjusted for the family of the items, by Holm's method by default (p_adjust). An item left with one level is not tested: its p cell shows a dash, and the note names it.

A design whose weights go negative, as linear calibration can make them, keeps its percentages, and its tests are withheld, with a warning (class spicy_negative_weights_no_test), as in table_categorical_svy().

What is absent

No interval or design effect per cell: a battery of five levels in three groups would carry thirty of each, and table_categorical_svy() gives them item by item. No column percentages, and no mean of the scale.

See also

table_battery() for the data-frame sibling, table_categorical_svy() for one block of rows per variable.

Examples

data(api, package = "survey")
dstrat <- survey::svydesign(
  id = ~1, strata = ~stype, weights = ~pw, data = apistrat, fpc = ~fpc
)
# Four yes-no items of the schools, one row each.
table_battery_svy(dstrat, select = c(awards, sch.wide, comp.imp, both))
#> Item battery
#> 
#>  Variable   │   No     Yes      n   
#> ────────────┼───────────────────────
#>  awards     │  36.1    63.9    200  
#>  sch.wide   │  17.2    82.8    200  
#>  comp.imp   │  34.4    65.6    200  
#>  both       │  36.1    63.9    200  
#> 
#> Note. Design: stratified (stype), with finite population correction; 197 degrees of freedom. Percentages are row percentages estimated under the design. Base: respondents who answered the item. n = observed (unweighted) count.

# By school type: the estimated percentages of each type and a
# design-based test per item.
table_battery_svy(
  dstrat,
  select = c(awards, sch.wide, comp.imp, both),
  by = stype
)
#> Item battery by stype
#> 
#>  Variable │ E No  E Yes  E n  H No  H Yes  H n  M No  M Yes  M n    p   
#> ──────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>  awards   │ 27.0  73.0   100  68.0  32.0   50   52.0  48.0   50   <.001 
#>  sch.wide │  9.0  91.0   100  48.0  52.0   50   30.0  70.0   50   <.001 
#>  comp.imp │ 25.0  75.0   100  66.0  34.0   50   52.0  48.0   50   <.001 
#>  both     │ 27.0  73.0   100  68.0  32.0   50   52.0  48.0   50   <.001 
#> 
#> Note. Design: stratified (stype), with finite population correction; 197 degrees of freedom. Percentages are row percentages estimated under the design. Base: respondents who answered the item. Item p-values, each item by group: design-based Pearson chi-squared (Rao-Scott second-order correction). Adjusted for 4 tests (Holm method). n = observed (unweighted) count.

# Long data frame.
head(table_battery_svy(
  dstrat,
  select = c(awards, sch.wide),
  by = stype,
  output = "long"
))
#>   variable  label group level .row_role  n pct test_type      p.value
#> 1   awards awards     E    No     level 27  27         F 2.082109e-06
#> 2   awards awards     E   Yes     level 73  73         F 2.082109e-06
#> 3   awards awards     H    No     level 34  68         F 2.082109e-06
#> 4   awards awards     H   Yes     level 16  32         F 2.082109e-06
#> 5   awards awards     M    No     level 26  52         F 2.082109e-06
#> 6   awards awards     M   Yes     level 24  48         F 2.082109e-06
#>   p_unadjusted
#> 1 2.082109e-06
#> 2 2.082109e-06
#> 3 2.082109e-06
#> 4 2.082109e-06
#> 5 2.082109e-06
#> 6 2.082109e-06
